items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: Interviewer mentions 'Dizzy' in a list of people the interviewee has played with, but the interviewee does not confirm playing with Dizzy, instead listing other musicians like Joe Newman, Ted Dunbar, and Frank Foster.

ctx.x: I’m trying to think about that. I think what happens, which happens today, is that people kind of know what you’re capable of. And they’ll call you if they think that you can fit the bill. I think that’s basically what happens you know.
Yeah. Let’s see, Herbie Mann and Dizzy and Joe Newman, I mean you’ve played with just about everybody, right?

Yeah, I had a wonderful time. I had a lot of wonderful gigs and some of my favorite gigs were with Joe Newman say for instance, very exciting, with Ted Dunbar playing guitar you know, Frank Foster. I’m still playing with Frank, he’s one of my all time favorites. A great writer, great player, great person to be with, be on the road with. And just a real homey kind of, very warm, wonderful person.
